title: BLOOM: Bit-Slice Framework for DNN Acceleration with Mixed-Precision
problem: INT4 quantization limited by outliers (high-magnitude values); existing outlier-aware compression adds complex serialization/deserialization logic that dominates execution time, reducing speedup.
motivation: Sub-INT8 quantization is necessary for model compression on edge hardware; but outlier handling complexity negates speedup gains.
method: Bit-slicing framework exploiting outlier-precision separation: outliers retain higher precision (INT8), normal values use INT4; interleaved bit-level storage exposes sparsity in high-precision components, enabling adaptive dataflow with minimal serialization overhead.
key_novelty: Bit-slicing mixed-precision architecture that decouples outlier/normal pathways to eliminate serialization bottleneck.
contributions: Bit-slice framework for mixed-precision DNN acceleration
Structured sparsity exploitation in interleaved INT4/INT8 values
1.2-4.0x speedup and 24.6%-71.3% energy reduction vs outlier-aware methods
limitations: Assumes outlier distribution known; applicability to models with irregular outlier patterns not discussed.
primary_theme: bit-slice mixed-precision for efficient INT4 DNN acceleration
